description: Six-panel composite of backscattered-electron (BSE) SEM micrographs of a hot-rolled Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic low-density steel at three hot-rolling reductions. The top row, (a-c), are lower-magnification images with 20 µm scale bars showing the micron-sized second-phase particles: bright polygonal/angular particles forming interrupted stringers and clusters, several in large agglomerates (notably a big blocky cluster in the lower-middle of (a) and a coarse blocky particle at the upper right of (c)), set in a grey polygonal austenite grain matrix that shows faint contrast bands. The bottom row, (d-f), are higher-magnification images with 300 nm scale bars showing the submicron-sized second phase: many small bright spherical/near-spherical particles dispersed through the austenite matrix and along grain boundaries. The samples are (a, d) HR45, (b, e) HR68 and (c, f) HR82. The particles appear bright because of their higher average atomic number relative to the austenite matrix. The figure demonstrates that two distinct particle populations — micron-sized polygonal particles aligned in rolling-direction bands and homogeneously dispersed submicron spherical particles — coexist in all three hot-rolled samples; no particle-size values are printed on the panels themselves.

subfigures.description: BSE-SEM micrograph of sample HR45, 20 µm scale bar. Bright polygonal/angular micron-sized particles arranged in roughly horizontal bands (stringers) with a prominent coarse agglomerate of angular bright particles in the lower-middle; faintly contrasting grey austenite grains.

BSE-SEM micrograph of sample HR68, 20 µm scale bar. Bright micron-sized polygonal particles concentrated in a horizontal stringer band running across the middle of the field, together with a few isolated bright particles; equiaxed grey austenite grains.

BSE-SEM micrograph of sample HR82, 20 µm scale bar. Bright micron-sized particles in a horizontal band across the upper-middle plus a large blocky bright particle at the upper right and scattered smaller particles; matrix shows faint darker and lighter grey banding.

Higher-magnification BSE-SEM micrograph of HR45, 300 nm scale bar. Numerous small bright spherical particles of varying size distributed over polygonal austenite grains; a few larger bright spheres are visible.

Higher-magnification BSE-SEM micrograph of HR68, 300 nm scale bar. Sparse-to-moderate population of small bright spherical particles dispersed in a matrix with several grains of differing grey contrast.

Higher-magnification BSE-SEM micrograph of HR82, 300 nm scale bar. Dense, broadly homogeneous dispersion of small bright spherical particles across the austenite matrix, with some slightly larger bright particles.

observations.observation: The figure is a 2-row x 3-column montage of six backscattered-electron SEM micrographs, all of the same steel in three different hot-rolling conditions.
Panels (a), (b) and (c) each carry a 20 µm scale bar, indicating the micron-sized-particle overview magnification.
Panels (d), (e) and (f) each carry a 300 nm scale bar, indicating the higher magnification used for the submicron-sized particles.

In (a-c) the micron-sized second phase appears as bright polygonal/angular particles that are not randomly placed but form interrupted chains/stringers roughly parallel to each other, consistent with alignment along the rolling direction.
In (d-f) the submicron-sized second phase appears as small bright spherical particles dispersed throughout the austenite matrix rather than in chains.

Bright particle contrast against the grey matrix is consistent with atomic-number (Z) contrast in backscattered-electron imaging, i.e. the particles have a higher average atomic number than the austenite.

The caption states that panels (a, d) correspond to HR45, (b, e) to HR68, and (c, f) to HR82, and that (a-c) show micron-sized while (d-f) show submicron-sized second-phase particles at higher magnification.
The citing text reports that the micron-sized polygonal particles lie in bands along the rolling direction at both grain boundaries and grain interiors, with sizes ranging from 1 to 25 µm.
The citing text reports mean submicron particle sizes of 261 ± 36 nm, 256 ± 42 nm and 259 ± 23 nm for HR45, HR68 and HR82 respectively.
The citing text reports submicron particle volume fractions of ~0.193%, ~0.201% and ~0.198% for HR45, HR68 and HR82 respectively.
The citing text identifies these precipitates as (Nb,Mo,W)C, with the intergranular ones located at austenite grain boundaries.
No numeric particle-size, volume-fraction or composition labels are printed inside any of the six panels; the only in-image quantitative marks are the scale bars.

measured_quantities: micron-sized particle size (1-25 µm, reported in citing text)
unreadable_items: Individual particle sizes cannot be measured from the panels at the supplied resolution; (d-f) particles are only 1-3 pixels across and no size annotations are printed.
No rolling-direction arrow or orientation marker is visible in any panel, so the rolling-direction alignment is inferred from the text, not read from the image.
